findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "submit_bid" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Submit a bid on an open job, as the authenticated user. You can't bid on your own job. You get one bid per job, ever: your bid amount cannot be edited afterward…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_job, get_messages, get_me, get_my_jobs, get_ratings, get_document · Private data: browse_jobs, get_document · Public sink: post_job, submit_bid, send_message, submit_rating, get_me.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_job, get_messages, get_me, get_my_jobs, get_ratings, get_document · Private data: browse_jobs, get_document · Public sink: post_job, submit_bid, send_message, submit_rating, get_me

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
